questions.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -9 & -18 & -3 \\ 0 & -10 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -10 & 0 \\ -18 & 18 & -36 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $P$ given above. Which of the following statements are true?

I. $\lambda =-1$ is an eigenvalue of $P$

II. $\lambda =-10$ is an eigenvalue of $P$

III. The eigenvalue $\lambda =-10$ has algebraic multiplicity $3$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,P-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
P-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & -9 & -18 & -3 \\ 0 & -10-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -10-\lambda  & 0 \\ -18 & 18 & -36 & -4-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(P-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Notice that we can expand the $4\times 4$ determinant across the $2$nd row, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(P-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & -9 & -18 & -3 \\ 0 & -10-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -10-\lambda  & 0 \\ -18 & 18 & -36 & -4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-10-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & -18 & -3 \\ 0 & -10-\lambda  & 0 \\ -18 & -36 & -4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, expanding the $3\times 3$ determinant across the $2$nd row, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-10-\lambda )\cdot (-10-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & -3 \\ -18 & -4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-10-\lambda )^{2}((-1-\lambda )(-4-\lambda )-54) & =0 \\ (\lambda +10)^{2}({\lambda }^{2}+5\lambda -50) & =0 \\ (\lambda +10)^{2}(\lambda +10)(\lambda -5) & =0 \\ (\lambda +10)^{3}(\lambda -5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the eigenvalues of $P$ are $\lambda =-10$ (with algebraic multiplicity $3$) and $\lambda =5.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."

questions.problem:
$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 7 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $B$ given above. Which of the following statements are true?

I. $\lambda =-5$ is an eigenvalue of $B$

II. $\lambda =-1$ is an eigenvalue of $B$

III. The eigenvalue $\lambda =-3$ has algebraic multiplicity $2$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,B-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
B-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-5-\lambda  & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 3-\lambda  & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 7 & -3-\lambda  & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(B-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Notice that we can expand the $4\times 4$ determinant across the $1$st column, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-5-\lambda  & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 3-\lambda  & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 7 & -3-\lambda  & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-5-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 0 & -2 \\ 7 & -3-\lambda  & 4 \\ 5 & 0 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, expanding the $3\times 3$ determinant across the $2$nd column, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-5-\lambda )\cdot (-3-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & -2 \\ 5 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-5-\lambda )\cdot (-3-\lambda )((3-\lambda )(-1-\lambda )+10) & =0 \\ (\lambda +5)(\lambda +3)({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +7) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Since $D<0$ for the polynomial ${\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +7$, we have that the only real eigenvalues are $\lambda =-5$ and $\lambda =-3$ (both with algebraic multiplicity $1$).

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

questions.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -8 & -4 \\ 3 & 8 & 3 \\ -6 & -10 & -3\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,B-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
B-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & -8 & -4 \\ 3 & 8-\lambda  & 3 \\ -6 & -10 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(B-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $1$st row, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & -8 & -4 \\ 3 & 8-\lambda  & 3 \\ -6 & -10 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 3 \\ -10 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}|-(-8)|\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ -6 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}|+(-4)|\begin{aligned}3 & 8-\lambda  \\ -6 & -10\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-5\lambda +6)+8(-3\lambda +9)-4(-6\lambda +18) & =0 \\ (-{\lambda }^{3}+4{\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -6)+(-24\lambda +72)-(-24\lambda +72) & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}+4{\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -6 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{3}-4{\lambda }^{2}+\lambda +6 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Determine all real eigenvalues $\lambda $ of the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -3 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,A-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -3-\lambda  & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is given by $det(A-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $1$st row, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -3-\lambda  & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-3-\lambda  & 3 \\ 2 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}|-(-1)|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}|+(-1)|\begin{aligned}1 & -3-\lambda  \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-{\lambda }^{3}-2{\lambda }^{2}+15\lambda )+(-5-\lambda )+(5+\lambda ) & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}-2{\lambda }^{2}+13\lambda -10 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{3}+2{\lambda }^{2}-13\lambda +10 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to solve this equation. We find the first root by testing some values. According to the rational zeros theorem, a list of good first guesses consists of all divisors of $10:$ 

$$
\pm 1,\pm 2,\pm 5,\pm 10
$$

Let's pick $x=1.$ Substituting to the characteristic equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(1)^{3}+2(1)^{2}-13(1)+10 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $\lambda =1$ is a root of the equation. So, we can factor $(\lambda -1)$ out of ${\lambda }^{3}+2{\lambda }^{2}-13\lambda +10$ using synthetic division:

| $1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $-13$ | $10$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | $↓$ | $1$ | $3$ | $-10$ |
|  | $1$ | $3$ | $-10$ | $0$ |

So, we obtain the following factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\lambda -1)({\lambda }^{2}+3\lambda -10) & =0 \\ (\lambda -1)(\lambda +5)(\lambda -2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=-5,$ $\,{\lambda }_{2}=1,\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}=2.$
